paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. The tomb is empty because Jesus kept His word, and that changes everything about how you hear what He says. The two men tell the women, "He is not here; He has risen!" and then send them back to what Jesus told them in Galilee: He would be crucified, and "on the third day rise again" (Luke 24:6-7). When Jesus says it, it happens, even when nobody around Him sees how.

Notice who gets this news first. It's the women who followed, watched where He was laid, and showed up with spices to do the small, faithful thing in front of them. Joseph of Arimathea did the same, a good man who stepped up to ask for the body of Jesus (Luke 23:50-52). Nobody in this passage had the whole picture, and I think that's the comfort, baker. God uses people who show up with what they have, and the tomb is where they find out He was already ahead of them.

Then comes the part that hits close to home. The apostles hear the best news ever told and it "seemed like nonsense" to them, but Peter still gets up and runs (Luke 24:11-12). He sees only linen cloths and goes home wondering, and I think that's an honest place to stand. Wondering is not the end of the road. If you have questions about what Jesus said, run toward His Word like Peter ran toward that tomb, because this story is FAR from done.
